 NRAI appointment under scrutiny after RTI contradicts shotgun coordinator’s credentials 
 NRAI president Kalikesh Narayan Singh Deo calls the disputed contract clauses ‘typos’, while a Delhi High Court petition challenges Amar Jang Singh’s appointment and raises questions about eligibility guidelines.
 Updated : Nov 17, 2026 11:15 IST , CHENNAI - 3 MINS READ 
 Santadeep Dey

 Amar Jang Singh (bottom left) and Kalikesh Narayan Singh Deo (bottom right) with the trap medallists during the 68th National Shooting Championship.
 | Photo Credit: NRAI
 Amar Jang Singh (bottom left) and Kalikesh Narayan Singh Deo (bottom right) with the trap medallists during the 68th National Shooting Championship.
 | Photo Credit: NRAI
 A Right to Information (RTI) request by national-level shooter Baber Khan has revealed conflicting reports about the credentials of Amar Jang Singh, a coordinator with the national shotgun squad, contracted through June 2029 at a monthly remuneration of ₹2 lakh.
 A notarised employment contract dated July 1, 2023, identifies him as a “National Level Shooter”, while interestingly a subsequent agreement dated March 1, 2025, describes him as an “International Level Shooter”. Both documents are in Sportstar’s possession.
 However, an official RTI response issued on January 22 by Nimit Chopra, the federation’s Public Information Officer, contradicts both claims. Nimit stated that “Mr. Amarjang Singh has not participated in any National/International competitions”, adding that he does not even have an International Shooting Sport Federation (ISSF) ID.
 If the RTI response is accurate, it raises questions about how the NRAI expects Amar Jang to “make himself/herself always available for providing his/her services under this Agreement to train the shooters/athletes of the Indian squad for International events/competitions,” as stipulated under Article 2.2.b of his employment contract.
 NRAI president Kalikesh Narayan Singh Deo has dismissed these contractual errors as minor oversight. “I think the contract had a few typos in it. And that’s really what it is. Amar Jang Singh is on the shotgun committee of ISSF. He is also judge and jury of the ISSF. He manages ISSF competitions. He was there at the recently concluded World Championship as well. So, as a manager, judge and jury, he is fully qualified. And even at the NRAI, he manages competitions. He is not a coach; he is not a person who shoots himself,” he told this publication.
 The Delhi High Court subsequently heard a writ petition (W.P.(C) 16456/2026) filed by domestic shooter Dr. Deepak Singh against the Union of India and the NRAI on Wednesday, November 4.
 ALSO READ: India’s air rifle coaches involved in public spat after Doha World Championship debacle 
 The petition sought a writ of quo warranto to declare Amar Jang’s appointment illegal and void from the outset. The petitioner’s counsel argued that Amar Jang and a few other appointees (skeet coach Neelanjana Ghosal and trap coach Vikram Chopra) do not meet the mandatory eligibility criteria laid down in the NRAI’s guidelines, despite being “personally involved” in selecting the national team.
 Kalikesh, however, explicitly claims Amar Jang isn’t involved in the selection process. He said, “The NRAI has a technical committee which frames policies and rules. He has been a part of the same for around 10 years now. Managing, detailing, scheduling, and rules are what he manages for the ISSF. He makes sure everybody is sticking to the rules when competitions are held. And he is very competent to do that because he does it not only for India but also for international competitions.
 “That said, he has nothing to do with the selection of the team. That’s done by the selection committee, which comprises the coaches, president and secretary general. No third person comes in there. Whoever has issues should raise ones which pertain to the conduct of competitions or rules. I think trying to pin it on individuals is just pettiness.”
 The Court has issued notice in the matter and scheduled the next hearing for January 20, 2027.
